case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 11-5-2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.57 of 2003)
full_judgment:
MD. NURUZZAMAN, J: This Civil Appeal, by leave, has arisen out of the judgment and order dated 11.05.2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil  Revision No.57 of 2003 making the Rule absolute and thereby set aside the judgment and decree dated 23.07.2002 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Brahmanbaria in Title Appeal No.74 of 1999 dismissing the appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and decree dated 19.04.1999 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Kasba, Brahmanbaria in Title Suit No.18 of 1997 dismissing the suit.
2. The respondent Nos.1-8 as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.18 of 1997 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Kasba, Brahmanbaria, impleading the appellant as defendants and respondent Nos.9-22 as others defendant and respondent No.23 as proforma defendant, praying for declaration of title to  the suit land and for recovery of khas possession therein.
3. Facts leading, to filing of this civil appeal, in short, are that, the suit plot No.638 and 639 along with on non suited plot No.643 measuring 39 decimals of land originally belonged to Samina Bibi which was finally published in her name in Cadastral Survey (in short, C.S.) Khatian and that the said Samena Bibi died leaving behind her only daughter Amena Khatun and thereafter Amena Khatun died leaving behind her daughter Malekernesa alias Maleka. While Maleka was owning and possessing the said plots, she transferred the entire land of plot no.643 by executing and registering deed of sale no.3219 dated 26.04.62 and 07 decimals of land from the suit plots by  executing and registering another deed of sale bearing no.4967 dated 6.12.1972 to the plaintiff no.4 Abdul Sobhan alias Sobhan Miah. After purchase he mutated his name and got Jama Separated in Separation Case No.224/83-84 by creating a separate Khatian No.982 and took a loan from the Janata Bank, Brahmanbaria Branch by mortgaging the said 07 decimals of land. Thereafter, Maleka Begum died leaving behind one son Abdul Hossain, father of plaintiff No. 5, who died leaving behind plaintiff nos.3-5 as his sons and daughter and thus the plaintiff nos.1-4 became the owners of 27 decimals of land in the suit plot by way of purchase and by inheritance. That in State Acquisition (in short, S.A.) operation, the suit property along with the property of plot no.643 has been  wrongly recorded in the name of one Aderjaman and other, predecessors of the defendants in khatian no.117. The plaintiff learnt about the wrong record in the S.A. Khatian on the basis of so-called partition suit no.172 of 1929. The defendant No.5 with help of other defendants forcibly entered into the plot no.638 on 30.09.96 and constructed two Dochala tin shade and 3 Chouchala tin shade house defying the objection raised by plaintiff no.3.
4. The defendant No.3 contested the suit by filing a written statement contending, inter alia, that the suit is barred by limitation and that the suit plot nos.638 and 639 along with non-suited plot no.643 measuring an area of 39 decimals of land belonged to Samina Bibi and  her name was rightly recorded in C.S. Khatian. Samina Bibi subsequently defaulted to pay rents and the Talukder was going to file a suit for realization of rent then Samina Bibi executed Istafanama deed dated 06.06.1920 and surrendered the property in favour of the landlord who settled the property to Munshi Mia, son of Nawaj Ali on 10.09.1921 and thus Munshi Mia became the sole owner of the land of the said 3 plots and has been possessing of the said land and prayed for dismissal of the suit.
5. On conclusion of the trial, the Trial Court, considering the evidences and documents on record, dismissed the suit by the judgment and decree dated 19.04.1999.
6. Feeling aggrieved, by the judgment and decree of the Trial Court, the plaintiffs as appellants preferred Title Appeal No.74 of 1999 before the learned District Judge, Brahmanbaria. On transfer, the said appeal was heard by the learned Additional District Judge, Court No.1, Brahmanbaria who by the judgment and decree dated 23-07-2002 disallowed the appeal and thereby affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial Court and decreed the suit.
7. Feeling aggrieved, by the judgment and decree dated 23.07.2002 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Brahmanbaria, the plaintiffs as petitioners  preferred Civil Revision No.57 of 2003 before the High Court Division and obtained the Rule.
8. In due course, a Single Bench of the High Court Division upon hearing the parties made the Rule absolute by the impugned judgment and order dated 11.05.2009 and thereby set aside the judgment and decree of the Courts below.
9. The defendant as petitioner herein feeling aggrieved by the impugned judgment and order dated 11.05.2009 of the High Court Division preferred Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1431 of 2009 before this Division and obtained leave, which, gave rise to the instant appeal.
10. Md. N.K. Saha, the learned Senior Counsel  appearing on behalf of the appellant submits that the High Court Division committed an error of law in disturbing the findings of facts arrived at by both the Courts below and on misreading of the evidence on record committed an error of law in holding that the plaintiffs did not mention the date of cause of action and the date of dispossession and also gave perverse finding upon non-consideration of the findings of facts recorded by the lower Appellate Court. He next submits that the High Court Division made the Rule absolute in finding that both the Courts below specially the Appellate Court being the last Court of facts misread the evidence on record that the plaintiff did not mentioned the date of cause of action and the date of dispossession and  also gave perverse finding in failing to consider that neither the Trail Court not the lower Appellate Court found that the plaintiffs have not mentioned the date of cause of action and date of dispossession, rather, both the Courts below found that the plaintiffs failed to prove the date of cause of action and date of dispossession, as such, the observation made by the High Court Division is perverse which is liable to be set aside. He finally submits that the Trial Court found that the plaintiff did not adduce any direct witness to prove alleged dispossession and the Appellate Court affirmed those findings but the High Court Division neither reversed those finding arrive at on consideration of material evidence on record nor gave any independent finding regarding to  the plaintiffs’ title, date of knowledge about S.A. Plot No.117, proof of alleged dispossession, limitation and, as such, the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. Hence, the instant appeal may kindly be allowed.
11. Mr. Md. Mazibar Rahman, the learned Advocate-on-Record appeared in the appeal by filing caveat. He supports the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division.
12. We have heard Mr. N.K. Saha, the learned Senior Counsel for the appellant. Perused the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division and other connected materials on record.
13. Leave was granted to examine the following reasons of the appellants,
“ The High Court Division committed an error of law in disturbing the findings of facts arrived at by both the Courts below and on misreading of the evidence on record committed an error of law in holding that the plaintiffs did not mention the date of cause of action and the date of dispossession and also gave perverse finding upon non-consideration of the findings of facts recorded by the lower appellate Court. …. Therefore, learned judge of the High Court Division committed an error of law in holding that the suit is not barred by limitation and also in finding that the plaintiffs did adduce direct  evidence to prove alleged dispossession.”
14. We will weigh up the materials on record as to whether judgment and order of the High Court Division is justified or erred which calls for interference by this Division.
15. It is the long standing settled cardinal principle of appreciation of evidence that finding of facts, whether concurrent or not, arrived at by the trial and lower appellate court is immune from interference in revision, except in certain well-defined circumstances such as non-consideration and misreading of material evidence affecting the merit of the case, or misconception, misapplication or misapprehension of law.
16. In these points this Division decided in the case of Md. Habibur Rahman Bhuiyan and Others Vs. Mosammat Galman Begum and Others reported in 2013 33 BLD (AD)93 as follows:
“When a finding of fact is based on consideration of the materials on record, those findings are immune from interference by the revisional Court except there is non-consideration or misreading of the material evidence on record. The High Court Division has no jurisdiction to sit on appeal over a finding of fact. It is concerned with the question as to whether the appellate court in giving a particular finding has committed any error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice or such finding is found to have resulted from glaring misconception of law or there is misreading or non-consideration of material evidence in arriving at such finding …………… This Division would also interfere with the judgment of the High Court Division or the Tribunal where a finding is reached without taking into consideration vital evidence or where the conclusions arrived at without consideration of the materials evidence or the finding which is inconsistent with the evidence on record. Apart from the above if this Division finds a substantial and grave injustice or if there exists special and exceptional circumstances it can exercise extra ordinary jurisdiction for doing 'complete justice' in any matter pending before it. This does not mean that in every petition or appeal this Division will exercise extraordinary jurisdiction and reassess the evidence on record as may be done in an appeal under clause (2) of Article 103.”
17. The same was reiterated in the case of Shamser Ali (Md) and others vs. Mosammat Kafizan Bibi, reported in 44 DLR(AD)231-
“The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division in Revision set aside the above findings of the lower  appellate Court on re-assessment of the oral and documentary evidences on record which he was not permitted under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure.”
18. In the instant case, on a diligent delving into the judgments of the Trial Court and lower Appellate Court it become obvious to us that the Trial Court reached into the decision as to that the pivotal assertion of the plaintiffs concerning the ancestral ownership of them over the suit land was disproved on the basis of proper appreciation of the evidences on record. Thereafter, lower Appellate Court affirmed the same findings on apposite evaluation of the materials on record.
19. To prove the case, plaintiffs’ side examined 4 (four) P.Ws. P.W.1, Tahera Begum, P.W.2, Abu Zandal, P.W.3, Safor Ali and P.W.4, Abdul Aziz.
20. P.W.1, Tahera Begum, in her testimony, stated that on 30.09.1996, the defendants illegally upon trespassing the suit land, erected 5 (five) tinshed houses on the Plot No.638. She has further testified that her sister, the defendant No.3 resisted them and tried to stop the erecting of the houses. She did not know the names of the labours, her sister, the defendant No.3 resides in the suit Plot. As such, she is fully acquainted with the facts of dispossession. She admitted that she and her husband, the defendant No.4 resides in Brahmanbaira.
21. It appears from the decree of the suit that the defendant No.3 is Mrs. Rahima Khatun, wife of late Dhon Miah. On carefully scrutiny it appears that this defendant No.3, Mrs. Rahima Khatun was not examined on the side of the plaintiffs, rather, others P.Ws. i.e. P.W.2, Abu Zandal, P.W.3, Safor Ali and P.W.4, Abdul Aziz. So, it is abundantly apparent on the face of the record that the defendant No.3 was not adduced as P.W. to prove the dispossession and erecting the houses on the suit property.
22. It is long line of catena that in a suit for recovery of khas possession, the plaintiffs must prove at first their possession with specific date with supporting evidences. In that case, he can later claim that they were dispossessed on specific date and time from the suit property. But on the four corners of the evidences, adduced by the plaintiffs, we do not find any such facts possession or depositions in the present case.
23. From these facts, it is crystal clear that the plaintiffs’ side was not able to prove the possession followed by dispossession of the plaintiffs by the defendants from the suit properties.
24. It is curtail principle of law that only in revisional jurisdiction, the High Court Division can interfere, if it is found that the Court of appeal below committed any error of law or procedural mistake and such errors have affected the merit of the case. The plaintiffs must prove his plaint case to succeed in the suit. The weakness of the defence’s case cannot be the ground to succeed or to prove the plaint case.
25. To support the our above mentioned views, we can rely upon the case of Md. Naimuddin Sarder @ Naimuddin Sarder Vs. Md. Abdul Kalam Biswas @ Md. Abul Kalam Basiruddin @ Abul Kalam Azad and another reported in 39 DLR (AD)237 whereupon this Division was held that-
“It is now well-established that the High Court Division can only invoke its jurisdiction under the said section if there is any error of law or procedure committed by the first appellate Court and such error has affected the merit of the decision, otherwise a finding of  fact, however wrong it might appear, cannot be interfered with in second appeal.”
“Plaintiff in order to succeed must establish his own case to obtain a decree and weakness of defendant’s case is no ground for passing a decree in favour of the plaintiff.”
26. As such, this Division finds no non- consideration or misreading of the material evidence on record or an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice or such finding is found to have resulted from glaring misconception of law or misconception, misapplication or misapprehension of law in the judgments and decisions of the Courts below.
<u>27. Rather, we find with sheer surprise that the High Court Division committed error of law in disturbing the concurrent findings of facts arrived at by both the Courts below and on misreading of the evidence on record committed an error of fact in holding that the Courts below reached in a finding that the plaintiffs did not mention the date of cause of action and the date of dispossession. The real scenario is in fact the contrary. We find that the Courts below did never mention that the plaintiffs did not describe the date of cause of action and the date of dispossession. Rather, the Courts below on proper appreciation of the materials on record rightly decided that the plaintiffs failed to prove the cause of action and the date of dispossession. Hence, we compelled to approve the submission of the learned Senior Counsel that the High Court Division gave appalling discovery upon non-consideration of the findings of facts recorded by the Courts below.</u>
<u>Accordingly, we find merit in submissions of the learned Senior Counsel for the appellants. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed. No order as to cost. The impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is set aside and that of the Trial Court and lower Appellate Court are hereby restored.</u>
End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated the 8th day of July, 2002 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.5722 of 2001)
full_judgment:
M. Enayetur Rahim, J: This appeal, by leave, is directed against the judgment and order dated 8-7-2002 passed by the High Court Division in writ petition No.5722 of 2001 arose from proceedings of Appeal Case Nos.1810 of 1995, 1811 of 1995, 1813 of 1995, 1812 of 1995, 1814 of 1995 and 1889 of 1995 under section 31 of State Acquisition and Tenancy Rules, 1955 (hereinafter referred as to Tenancy Rules,1955) which was restored after setting aside the earlier order of dismissal.
2. The facts, relevant for disposal of the instant appeal are as follows:
The present appellants filed Writ Petition No.5722 of 2001 before the High Court Division challenging the proceedings of appeal Nos.1810 of 1995, 1812 of 1995, 1813 of 1995, 1814 of 1995 and 1889 of 1995 under rules 31 of the Tenancy Rules, 1995.
3. In the writ petition it was contended, inter-alia, that the name of the appellants recorded correctly in respect of disputed land situated under Bogura Settlement Zone. Against such record-of-rights some persons raised objection under rule 30 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955, which was ultimately rejected. Thereafter Appeal Case Nos.1810/95, 1811/95, 1813/95, 1812/95, 1814/95 and 1889/95 under rule 31 of the said Rules were dismissed by the Appellate Authority by an order dated 24-8-2000 on the ground of limitation. Eventually, one Rokyea Begum filed an application before the Ministry of Land and on the basis of the said application writ-respondent No.2, Director of Lands after making an inquiry set-aside the earlier order of dismissal of the appeals without serving any notice to the appellants and appointed respondent No.3, Assistant Settlement officer for re-hearing of the appeals. Consequently, the proceedings of all of the 5 (five) appeals were again started. The appellants without finding any other alternative remedy compelled to file the Writ Petition challenging the proceeding of said appeals.
4. The writ-respondent Nos.5 and 6 contested the writ petition by filing Affidavit-in-Opposition contending, inter-alia, that, the writ-petitioners-appellants filed an application for setting aside the order of restoration passed by the Director, Land Records before the Director General, Land Records and Surveys on 7-10-2001 and without waiting for the result of the said application filed the Writ Petition on 15-10-2001 which is not maintainable and is liable to be discharged. They further contended that the Director of land Records in exercising the power conferred upon him as per provision of Rule 44 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 restored the appeal cases. It was further contended that, the Director, Land Records in due exercise of his power set-aside the dismissal order of the appeals and passed a legal and valid order for re-hearing of the appeals by a competent Assistant Settlement Officer under Bogura Zonal settlement Office and hence, there is no illegality in passing the order of restoration. It was further contended that, at the time of attestation, the attestation officer on the basis of a false and fabricated deed of gift dated 16-6-1942 deleted the names of some heirs, who raised objection under Rule 30 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 and the objection officer illegally rejected the same and against the said rejection order they filed the appeals within date but the Authority has been wrongly dismissed the appeals solely on ground of limitation on 21-8-2000. Against the order of dismissal the writ-respondent No.5 filed an application before the Ministry of Land who forwarded the said application to the Director General, Land Records and Surveys. The Director General, Land Records and Surveys ordered Director, Land Records to take necessary action for disposal of the matter. The Director, Land Records ordered the Zonal Settlement Officer, Bogura for disposal of the appeals after re-hearing the same as because the appeals were filed within the limitation period. But the writ-respondent No-5 filed an application before the Director, Land Records to the effect that they would not get justice at Bogura Settlement Office and hence on 3-9-2001 the said officer passed an order to settle the appeals by the Assistant Settlement Officer, Zonal Settlement Office, Dhaka.
5. A Division Bench of the High Court Division after hearing the said Rule by the impugned judgment and order dated 8-7-2002 discharged the same.
6. Feeling aggrieved by the said judgment and order, the writ-petitioner's preferred civil petition for to appeal No.1601 of 2002 before this Division and eventually leave was granted.
7. Mr Qumrul Hoque Siddique, learned Advocate, appearing for the appellants having referred to Rules 31, 32, 42, 44 and 42A of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 submits that once appeal has been disposed of on contest under Rule 31 of the Tenancy Rules 1955, no review or other application lies and the settlement authority has no jurisdiction to re-open the matter other than to send to draft publication khatian of final publication under Rule 32 of the said Rules. Even rule 42 does not empower the settlement officer to sit and act as an appellate authority over the appellate order passed under Rule 31 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955.
8. Mr Hoque further submits that in the instant case no allegation of fraud has been proved, thus the order passed by the Director of Land Records is absolutely illegal and without lawful authority and the High Court Division in passing the impugned order failed to consider this legal aspect and, as such, the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set-aside.
9. Mr Hoque also submits that Director of Land Records and Surveys having been upgraded to Director General of Land Records and the Director of Land Records being a sub-ordinate officer, the exercise of power under Rule 44 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 by the said Director of Land Records is illegal and without jurisdiction.
10. Per contra, Mr Probir Neogi, learned Senior Advocate, appearing for the respondent Nos.5(a)-(d) and 6 submits that the High Court Division correctly held that the Director of land Records and the Director of Land Records and Survey is the same officer, when this officer performs his duty as regards the matter of land records only, he is designated as Director of Land Records, So, it is not acceptable at all that the Director of Land Records is not authorized to exercise the power of Rule 44 of Tenancy Rules. The correctness of the view taken by the High Court Division could be further clear from rule 44 which contemplates the powers of Revenue-Officers under Chapter XIV of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1955.
11. Mr Necigi further submits that a complaint made by Rokeya Begum [predecessor of respondents No. 5(a)-(d)] to the Ministry of Land would clearly show that deprivation of female heirs in the district of Bogura by some Revenue and Settlement Officers led by the then Zonal Settlement Officer has been categorically alleged with material particulars, and the Government in the Ministry of Land taking into consideration the entire perspectives and facts of the case directed the Directorate of Land Records and Surveys to look into the matter, who passed the order impugned in the writ petition.
12. Mr Neogi having referred to the memo No. ত্বঃ গরঃ ২৩/৯৫/খন্ড-১)১৬৬৬ তারিখ ২৩-৮-২০০১ issued by the Director, Land Records addressed to the zonal settlement office, Bogura submits that on an inquiry it was found that fraud had committed in disposing the 05 appeals in question and thus, the competent authority cancelled the orders and directed the competent settlement officer to hear the appeals afresh. The above order was passed by the Director, Land Records within its jurisdiction and thus, the instant appeal is liable to dismissed.
13. We have considered the rival submissions of the learned Advocates for the respective parties, perused the impugned judgment, the materials placed before us as well as the relevant provisions of law.
14. To determine the issue involved in the present case it is necessary to peruse rule 42A of the Tenancy Rules 1955, which is as follows:
142A. Correction of fraudulent entry before final publication of record-of-rights—The Revenue-officer, with the additional designation of 'Settlement Officer' shall, on receipt of an application or on receipt of an official report for the correction of an entry that has been procured by fraud in record-of-rights before final publication thereof, after consulting relevant records and making such other enquiries as he deems necessary, direct excision of the fraudulent entry and his act in doing so shall not be open to appeal. At the same time, the Revenue-officer shall make the correct entry after giving the parties concerned a hearing and recording his finding in a formal proceeding for the purpose of future reference.
15. This Division in the case of Bhawal Raj of Wards Estate vs Rasheda Begum, reported in 15 BLC (AD) 115 has held to the effect:
"After final publication of the record-of-right, after the SA Survey the only mode tor correction of the same was through it Court and thus subsequent to preparation of SA record-of-right, the RS record-of-right was prepared and after final publication thereof the mode for correction of any wrong entry appearing in the RS record was through Civil Court and without moving the Civil Court no correction in recent records of right is lawful or permissible and, as such, the draft record-of-right in the instant case having been prepared following the preparation of the SA and RS records in accordance with law, the attempts of the leave petitioner for correction under Rules 30 and 31 of the State Acquisition Rules,1955 have failed. The plain reading of the application dated 14-7-2002 allegedly filed under Rule 42A of the State Acquisition Rules, 1955, ex-facie appears to be a vague application, inasmuch as the said post contains no specific allegation of any act of fraud and it is the settled principle of law that an application, not having disclosed any act of fraud in its body, is not entertainable and  liable to be rejected."
16. Further in Civil Appeal No. 2 of 2004, Government of Bangladesh and others vs Shamsul Haque and another, this Division has also held that;
"From the order of the Director General, it appears that there was no  finding or observation of the Director General that the writ-petitioner-respondents managed to procure the entry  in the record-of-right by practicing fraud or entry was fraudulent one or that he  consulted the relevant records or that made  other enquires or that gave the parties  concerned a hearing concerned a hearing in  as much as Rule 42A of the Rules  empowered the Director General to correct  the entry after due compliance of the aforesaid legal requirements. Rule 42 provided that a Revenue Officer appointed with the additional designation of a "Settlement Officer" may, at any time before the publication of final record-of-rights, direct that any portion of the proceedings referred to in rules 28 to 32 in respect of a district, or local area, should be cancelled and that the proceedings should be taken up fresh from such stage as he may direct. But in the instant proceeding, as it appears from the order of the Director General, that the provisions of Rule 42A and 42 had not been followed, that is, it is apparent from the order of the Director General itself that the same was unlawful."
17. In view of the above settled proposition it is clear that a Revenue-officer, with the additional designating of 'settlement officer' has got the authority/jurisdiction to re-open an appeal if on receipt of an application or on receipt of official report for the correction of an entry that has been procured by fraud in record-of-rights before final publication thereof, after consulting relevant records and making such other enquires as he deems necessary, direct excision of fraudulent entry and at the same time, revenue officer has got the power to make the correct entry after giving the parties concerned a hearing and recording his findings.
18. Thus, it is crystal clear that if fraud has been done in recording of right before final publication thereof, the Revenue Officer can hear the matter afresh after consulting relevant records, making such other enquiry necessary, if he deems and giving opportunity of being heard of the parties.
19. Rule 41 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 provides power of settlement office, which is as follows:
"41. Power of Settlement Officer of withdraw and transfer cases:—A Revenue-officer appointed with the additional designation of "Settlement Officer" may also withdraw from the file of any Assistant Settlement Officer or Revenue-officer subordinate to him any of the proceedings under Chapter XVII and may dispose of them himself or transfer them for disposal to any other Assistant Settlement Officer or Revenue Officer subordinate to him."
20. Mr Hoque has raised another issue that Director of Land Records has no authority to pass an order pursuant to the Rule 44 of Rules, 1955 as the said post has been upgraded as Director General of Land Records and Surveys.
21. Section 44 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 runs as follows;
"44. Powers vested in Director of Land Records and Surveys:—In respect of all operations under Chapter XVII of the Act which have been placed under the administrative control of the Director of Land Records and Surveys, Bangladesh, he may discharge all the functions of a Revenue-Officer under the said Chapter and shall have all the powers of a Settlement Officer under rules 36, 38,39, 40, 41, 42, 42A and 42B."
<u>22. Upon perusal of the above rule it is clear that the Director of Land Records and Surveys has been vested with the power to discharge all functions of a Revenue Officer and shall have all powers of Settlement Officer under rule 42A along with some other rules in respect of all operation under chapter XVII of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act.</u>
23. In the instant case it reveals from the record that predecessors of the present Respondents No.5(a)-(d), Rokeya Begum, filed a compliant before the Ministry of Land regarding the alleged fraudulent entry in the record and thereafter Ministry of Land forwarded the same to Director General, Land Records and Surveys who ordered the Director, Land Records to dispose of the matter. Thereafter Director, Land Records after making an enquiry on the allegation made by Rokeya Begum and upon consideration of the said enquiry report he set-aside the orders passed in 05 appeals and directed a competent officer to hold hearing of the appeals in question.
24. The letter dated 23-8-2001 contains the decision of Director, Land Records runs as follows:
গণপ্রজাতন্ত্রী বাংলাদেশ সরকার
ভূমি রেকর্ড ও জরিপ অধিদপ্তর
তেজগাও, ঢাকা-১২০৮।
স্বারক নং-ত্বঃজরঃ২৩/৯৫/খন্ড-১)১৬৬৬
তারিখঃ ২৩-৬৮-২০০১
প্রাপকঃ জোনাল সেটেলমেন্ট অফিসার, বগুড়া।
বিষয়ঃ বগুড়া জোনের আক্কেলপুর উপজেলার ১নং রুকিন্দীপুর মৌজার ১৮১০/৯৫, ১৮১১/৯৫, ১৮১২/৯৫, ১৮১৩/৯৫, ১৮১৪/৯৫ এবং ১৮৮৯/৯৫ নং আপীল কেসের পুনঃশুনানী প্রসঙ্গে ।
জনৈকা রোকেয়া বেগম জং ময়েন উদ্দিন সরকার এবং অন্যান্যের উল্লিখিত আপীল কেসগুলির পুনঃশুনানীর আবেদন এর পরিপ্রেক্ষিতে সংশ্লিষ্ট আপীল কেসনথি, আপীল রেজিস্ট্রার আপত্তি রেজিস্ট্রার, কোর্ট ফি রেজিস্ট্রার, দরখাস্তকারীর পক্ষের প্রদর্শিত আপীল কেস দাখিলের রশিদ এবং অন্যান্য কাগজপত্র পরীক্ষা এবং পর্যালোচনা করা হয় । দেখা যায় যে, ১৮১০/৯৫, ১৮১১/৯৫, ১৮১২/৯৫, ১৮১৩/৯৫, ১৮১৪/৯৫ এবং ১৮৮৯/৯৫ নং আপীল কেস দাখিলে কোনরূপ তামাদি হয় নাই । অথচ, আপীল কেস ৫ (পাঁচ) টি-তে তামাদি দেখাইয়া খারিজ করিয়া দেওয়া হইয়াছে।
১৮৮৯৫ নং আপীল কেসটি ২২-৭-৯৫ ইং তারিখে দাখিল করায় উহা ৪১২ মাসে তামাদি হইয়াছে দেখা যায় । ১৮৮৯/৯৫ নং আপীল কেসের প্রথম দিনের শুনানীতে বিজ্ঞ আপীল অফিসার লিখিয়াছেন “আপীল মোকদ্দমাটি ২ মাস ২৬ দিনের তভামাদিতে দায়ের করা হইয়াছে। তামাদি মওকুফ করা হইয়াছে ।” কিন্তু বিজ্ঞ আপীল অফিসার গত ২৪-৮-২০০০ ইং তারিখে ১৮৮৯/৯৫ নং আপীল কেসটি ৩ মাস ১৮ দিন এবং ১৮১১/৯৫ নং আপীল কেসটি ২ মাস ৫ দিন তামাদি দেখাইয়া খারিজ করিয়াছেন যাহা স্ববিরোধীতাপূর্ণ দেখা যায়। উল্লেখ্য, ১৮১১/৯৫ এবং ১৮৮৯/৯৫ নং আগীল কেস ২টি একত্রে শুনানী দেওয়া হইয়াছে ।
উল্লিখিত আপীল কেসগুলি তামাদি না হওয়া স্বতেেও তামাদি দেখাইয়া খারিজ করিয়া দেওয়ায় পৈ্রিক সম্পত্তিতে দাবীদার দরখাস্তকারীগণ ভীবণ ভাবে ক্ষতিগ্রস্থ হইয়াছে এবং উল্লিখিত আপীল কেসগুলির নিষ্পত্তিতে মারাত্মক ধরনের বে-আইনী এবং অনিয়ম করা হইয়াছে দেখা যায় ।
এমতাবস্থায়, ন্যায় বিচার এবং নির্ভুল রেকর্ড প্রণয়নের স্বার্থে বগুড়া জোনের আক্কেলপুর উপজেলার ১নং রুকিন্দীপুর মৌজার ১৮১০/৯৫, ১৮১১/৯৫, ১৮১২/৯৫, ১৮১৩/৯৫, ১৮১৪/৯৫ এবং ১৮৮৯/৯৫ নং আপীল কেসের ২৪-৮-২০০০ ইং তারিখের রায় ১৯৫৫ সনের প্রজাস্বত্ বিধিমালার ৪৪নং বিধিতে প্রদত্ত ক্ষমতাবলে এতদ্বারা বাতিল করা হইল। ১৮৮৯/৯৫ নং আপীল কেসের তামাদি ১৯০৮ সনের তামাদি আইন এর বিধানমতে মওকুফ করা হইল। উক্ত আপীল কেসগুলি একজন বিশ্বস্ত এবং অভিজ্ঞ সহকারী সেটেলমেন্ট অফিসার ছারা (প্রাক্তন আপীল অফিসার ব্যতীত) জোনাল সেটেলমেন্ট অফিসার বগুড়ার শুনানী দিয়া নিষ্পত্তি করিবার প্রয়োজনীয় পদক্ষেপ গ্রহণ করিতে তাহাকে নির্দেশ প্রদান করা হইল। ইহা অত্যন্ত জরুরী । জনস্বার্থে ত্র আদেশ জারী করা হইল ।
স্বাঃ/
(মোঃ মঞ্জুরুল ইসলাম)
পরিচালক ভেমি রেকর্ড)
25. From the above, it is clear that fraudulent act had been committed in disposal of the appeal Nos.1810/95, 1811/95, 1813/95, 1812/95, 1814/95 and 1889/95 under rule 31 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 and concerned authority i.e. Director Land Records after holding enquiry passed the necessary orders, which is within the ambit of rule 42A and 44 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955.
26. From ‘ভূমি রেকর্ড ও জরিপ অধিদপ্তর কর্মকর্তাদের দায়িত্���’ as produced before this court by Mr Hogue, it transpires that Director-General of Land Records and Surveys Directorate has been empowered to ‘অধীনস্থ কর্মকর্তাদেরকে প্রয়োজনীয় ক্ষমতা অর্পণের আদেশ প্রদান।’ And Director, Land. Records is bound to do perform any assignment delegated to him by the Director-General. Thus, in exercising power under rule 42A and 44, the Director, Land Records did not commit any illegality; rather he passed the same within his jurisdiction. Thus, we find no substance in the submission of Mr Hoque, that the Director, Land Records had passed the order exceeding his jurisdiction.
27. Having considered the facts and circumstances of the present case coupled with the settled proposition of law by this Division, we find no substance in the appeal.
Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed without any order as to cost.
End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 11-8-2010 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.3201 of 2001)
full_judgment:
Md Nuruzzaman, J: This Civil Appeal, by leave, has arisen out of the judgment and order dated 11-8-2010 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.3201 of 2001 making the Rule absolute and setting aside the judgment and decree dated 5-6-1996 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, First Court (now joint District Judge), Panchaghar in Other Appeal No.12 of 1995 allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree dated 29-4-1993 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Debiganj, Panchaghar, in Other Suit No.17 of 1993 dismissing the suit.
2. Facts leading to filing of this civil appeal, in short, are that:
The appellants herein as the plaintiffs instituted Other Suit No.17 of 1993 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Debiganj, Panchaghar against the defendants-respondents praying for a decree declaring the order under Memo No.SA/Misc. Case No.XII/20/87-88/871(10) dated 26-7-1993 in pursuance of the Land Ministry's Memo No.6-E-10/73/710(19)L&B Estbt. dated 29-11-1973, passed by the defendant No.1 cancelling of the Genuineness Certificate issued on 29-4-1989 in favour of the plaintiffs and the registered deed No.4398 dated 20-5-1989 being obtained in Miscellaneous Exchange Case No.878/8/66-67 which was renumbered as Miscellaneous Exchange Case No.172/8/85-86 was illegal, void, inoperative and not binding upon the plaintiffs.
3. Plaintiffs' case, in short, was that they originally were inhabitants of village—Ujakbari, Police Station—Malbazar, District—Zalpaiguri within West Bengal, India at present. They being felt insecure of their lives and properties in India exchanged their properties in India with the suit land belonging to Shochidananda Sarkar of the then East Pakistan now Bangladesh who executed an exchange deed on 28-12-1960 along with an irrevocable power of attorney in favour of died plaintiffs for the suit lands. Plaintiffs for their properties in India executed and registered a sale deed in 1960 in favour of Shochidananda Sarkar. The irrevocable power of attorney was re-authenticated in the East Pakistan. After such exchange the plaintiffs entered into possession and had been possessing the suit lands. Plaintiffs came to the East Pakistan in 1964. Later on the Ministry of Land, Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh by its Circular No.6-E-10/ 73/ 710(19) dated 29-11-1973 empowered all the Deputy Commissioners of the concerned districts to regularize of the unregistered exchange deeds of the Indian Muslim refugees. Pursuant to said Circular dated 29-11-1973, plaintiffs filed Miscellaneous Exchange Case No.878/8/66-67 before the Deputy Commissioner, Dinajpur for regularization of their exchange deed and on which an enquiry was held. On re-organization of the district administration, the said case was transferred to the newly created Panchagarh district and re-numbered as Miscellaneous Exchange Case No.172/8/85-86. Defendant No.1, Deputy Commissioner, Panchagarh upon enquiry and perusing the papers/documents of the plaintiffs issued a Genuineness Certificate dated 29-4-1989 and the defendant No.3, Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Panchagarh on behalf of the defendant No.1 executed and registered the deed of transfer No.4398 dated 20-5-1989. Subsequently, the defendant Nos.9 to 17 as plaintiffs instituted Other Suit No.12 of 1989 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Debiganj praying for a decree for cancellation of the said registered deed No.4398 dated 20-5-1989 which upon hearing was dismissed. The said defendants as appellants preferred Title Appeal No.20 of 1990 which was also dismissed. The defendants having lost in both the Courts moved the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.8052 of 1991. During the pendency of the Civil Revision No.8052 of 1991, knowing the said facts that the defendant No.1 issued a notice upon the plaintiff. No.2 asking the plaintiffs to show cause as to why the Genuineness Certificate dated 29-4-1989 and registered deed No.4398 dated 20-5-1989 would not be cancelled, the said notice was served upon other plaintiffs. Plaintiff No.2 pursuant to notice appeared before the authority, prayed for time to show cause but the defendant No.1 without giving any opportunity to submit the reply passed an order on 26-7-1993 for cancellation of the Genuineness Certificate and the deed of the plaintiffs. The defendant Nos.1, 4 to 8 and 9 to 17 in collusion with each other threatened to dispossess the plaintiffs from the suit lands and the homestead thereon on 04.08,1993 and hence the suit.
4. Defendant Nos.1 to 7 and the defendant Nos.10 to 15 contested the suit by filing 2 sets of separate written statements denying the averments made in the plaint contending inter alia that their common case were that the suit land belonged to Shochidananda Sarkar and he left the then East Pakistan for India and did not exchange his lands in Bangladesh i.e. the suit lands, with the plaintiffs or anyone else. The plaintiffs in order to grab the suit lands created a forged and fictitious deed of exchange and an irrevocable power of attorney and managed to get the Genuineness ' Certificate issued by the defendant No.1 for the so-called exchange deed. The local people having come to know about of the said forged and fictitious deed of exchange and the power of attorney made complaint to the concerned authority. Upon which the then Revenue Deputy Collector, Panchagarh causing physical enquiry submitted his report finding that the deed of exchange and the power of attorney was forged and fictitious and the said deed was comprised of khash land of the Government. Their further case was that as the said Shocidananda Sarkar left for India leaving his properties uncared for, the Government declaring the suit land abandoned settled to some lands therein to Gent Barmanand others, the bargadars of Shocidananda Sarkar in various Settlement Cases who had been possessing the suit lands on payment of rents. In the suit lands there were Government Food Godown, Sub-Registrar Office, residence of Government Medical Officer and Thana Health Inspector. As the plaintiffs were engaged in grabbing the Government properties, notice was served upon the plaintiffs asking them to show cause as to why the Genuineness Certificate issued on 29-4-1989 and the registered deed No.4398 dated 20-5-1989 regularizing the exchange deed in their favour would not be cancelled. The plaintiffs having received the notice appeared and prayed for time to show cause and time was granted but they did not show any cause. Consequently, the defendant No.1 passed the impugned order dated 26-7-1993 for cancellation of the Genuineness Certificate issued earlier and the registered deed rightly and properly. The defendant Nos.10 to 15 purchased some lands out of the suit lands from the Geru Bartman and others and their successors by Kabalas and had been possessing the same erecting dwelling house thereon. Plaintiffs had no right, title, interest and possession over the suit lands and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed.
5. On conclusion of the trial, the learned Assistant Judge, Debiganj, Panchagar after hearing the parties, considering the evidences and documents on record, dismissed the suit by its judgment and decree dated 29-4-1995.
6. Feeling aggrieved by the judgment and decree dated 29-4-1995 passed by the trial Court in Title Suit No.17 of 1993, the appellants-plaintiffs preferred Title Appeal No.12 of 1995 before the learned District Judge, Panchagar and it was transferred to the learned Sub-Judge (now Joint District Judge), 1st Court, Panchagar, who by his judgment and decree dated 5-6-1996 allowed the appeal and thereby reversed the judgment and decree of the trial Court.
7. Feeling aggrieved by the judgment and decree dated 5-6-1996 passed by the learned Sub-Judge (now Joint District Judge), 1st Court, Panchagar in Title Appeal No.12 of 1995, the defendants-petitioners preferred Civil Revision No.3201 of 2001 before the High Court Division.
8. In due course, a Single Bench of the High Court Division, upon hearing the parties, made Rule absolute by the impugned judgment and order dated 11-8-2010.
9. The heirs of the plaintiff No.2 as petitioners herein feeling aggrieved by the impugned judgment and order dated 11-8-2010 of the High Court Division preferred Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.2691 of 2010 before this Division and obtained leave which gave rise to the instant appeal.
10. Mr Probir Niego, the learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellants submits that sub-section (6) of section 9 of Arpito Shompotti Pratyarpan Ain, 2001 (Act No. XVI of 2001) (as amended by Arpito Shompotti Pratyarpan (Songshodhon) Ain, 2011 (Act No.23 of 2011)having provided- "(৬) এই ধারার অধীনে ক-তফসিলে বর্ণিত এবং গেজেটে প্রকাশিত সম্পত্তির তালিকায় অন্তর্ভুক্ত নহে এমন কোন সম্পত্তি বলিয়া গণ্য হইবে না এবং উহাতে অর্পিত সম্পত্তি হিসাবে সরকারের কোন স্বত্ব, স্বার্থ, অধিকার বা দায়-দায়িত্ব থাকিবে না।” the suit property having not been included in the list of vested properties, the petitioners claiming through Government are stopped by operation of law from claiming the suit property to be vested property. He further submits that the Government having not moved the High Court Division against the appellate Court's decision which amounts to conceding to the said decision, the High Court Division was wrong in allowing the Government to appear in the civil revision filed by private parties as petitioner No.7. He next submits that High Court Division on the one hand, held that the petitioners in Civil Revision No.3201 of 2001 (who were plaintiffs in Other Suit No.12 of 1089) had no locus standi to challenge the registered deed No.4398 dated 20-5-1989, and on the other hand, made the Rule absolute obtained by the same persons having no locus standi, and thereby committed patent error of law. He finally submits that the instant case involves an important question of law concerning public interest namely, when a suit seeking cancellation of certain decision/ document has failed all through in trial Court, appellate Court and in the High Court Division in revision whether the same decision/ document can be cancelled by the administrative order inasmuch as if it is allowed there will be a no sanctity of judicial decisions. Mr Niogi also pointed out that the defendant Nos.9 to 17 impleaded herein as respondents, instituted an Other. Suit bearing No. 12 of 1989 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Debiganj praying for a decree for cancellation of the impugned registered deed No. 4398 dated 20-5-1989 as plaintiffs, which upon hearing was dismissed. Against which as appellants, they preferred Title Appeal no. 20 of 1990 which was also dismissed. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the decree and judgment the same defendants moved the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.8052 of 1991. It is evident from the paper book that the cancellation of Genuineness Certificate and registered deed of transfer was made on 25-7-1993, on the other hand, the aforementioned rule was discharged in Civil Revision No. 8052 of 1991 on 16-3-1998 i.e., the impugned cancellation of deeds was made when the matter was sub judice in a civil revision before the High Court Division. Such acts of the executive authority have been deprecated by the Appellate Division in Syed Mohammad Salem Azam vs Bangladesh, 47 DLR (AD) 38. Mr Neogi candidly pointed out that an important question of law concerning public interest is involved in this case to the effect that defendants No. 9-17 after failing to get the declaration that the exchange deed, Genuineness Certificate and registered deed of transfer are void in a suit, appeal, and revision; on their application for the self-same relief on the self-same ground, can the Government cancel those documents when the judiciary in three stages including the High Court Division in Revision refused to do so? It is so for the simple reason that if it is permitted, there will be no sanctity of judicial decision. And that will make avenue to overruling of judicial decision by executive judgment which is simply beyond the constitutional scheme of the rule of law. In other words, there will be executive review of judicial decision, which is unheard of, and beyond the contemplation of our constitutional scheme.
11. After a prolonged enquiry in two stages starting from 1966, Genuineness Certificate was issued in 1989; thereafter the abovementioned Other Suit No. 12 of 1989 for declaration that exchange deed is void, and the Appeal and Revision therefrom failed, and on the application of unsuccessful plaintiffs of the said suit, serving a notice upon only one plaintiff, cancellation of Genuineness Certificate and registered deed of transfer by an administrative order is not only illegal, it is arbitrary. Mr Neogi in supports of his submissions relied upon on the following precedents:—
(a) in the case of Syed Mohammad Salem Azam and others vs The Secretary, Ministry of Works, Government of Bangladesh and others reported in 47 DLR (AD) 38, (b) in the case of Hashem (Md) vs Bangladesh and others reported in 43 DLR 109, (c) in the case of Dark Chandra Majhi vs Atahar Ali Howlader and others reported in 8 BLC (AD) 67, (d) in the case of Haidernessa and another vs Monowara Begum and others reported in 1996 BLD (AD) 280, (e) in the case of Habibur Rahman Bhuiyan (Md) and others vs Galman Begum and others reported in 64 DLR (AL)) 133, (f) in the case of Shamser Ali (Md) and others vs Mosammat Kafizan Bibi reported in 44 DLR (AD) 231, (g) in the case of Satyadliyan Ghosal and others vs Smt. Deorajin Debi and another reported in AIR 1960 (X) 941.
12. Hence, the instant appeal should be allowed.
13. Mr AM Amin Uddin, the learned Attorney-General with Mr SM Monir, Additional Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the respondent Nos.1 and 2; Mr Zulfiqur Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent No.10(i); Mr Nurul Amin, the learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent Nos.11(iii)-11(iv) and Mr Md Shahidul Islam, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent Nos.14(kha)-14(gha) made submissions in support of the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division.
14. Mr AM Aminuddin, the learned Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the respondent Nos.1 and 2 submits that there is a provision in the deed of transfer in question dated 25-8-89 that "if it is found that fraud has been practiced upon the Deputy Commissioner to grant the above mentioned genuineness certificate or it is found that any of the deeds and papers submitted by 1st party showing exchange of his Indian properties is fraudulent than it will be lawful for the 2nd party to determine this deed of conveyances by a written notice and the 1st party shall have no right or title to the properties described in the scheduled of this deed". Subsequently, the Deputy Commissioner being found that the appellants making fraud upon the Deputy Commissioner obtained the genuineness certificate and the registered deed, thus after issuing the show cause notice upon these appellants rightly and legally cancelled those documents, and, as such, the judgment of the High Court Division is sustainable in law. He further submits that as the defendant petitioner Nos.1 to 6 being the lessees of the Government of Bangladesh, thus the High Court Division rightly and legally transposed the Government as petitioner No.7 in the Civil Revision by an order dated 6-4-2010. Moreso, the appellants not challenging the said order of transposing dated 6-4-2010 before this Division, so, now the appellants have no right to make any dispute or question to the said order and are stopped in making or raising any question about that order of transposing. Thus, the impugned judgment and order is sustainable in law.
15. He next submits that the Courts below found that some leasee of the Government and some office of the defendant respondents Government are being situated in the land in question and thus, the plaintiffs are not in possession of the suit land, thus, the suit for simple declaration is not maintainable under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act without prayer for consequential relief and hence, the appeal is liable to be dismissed. He finally submits that the plaintiff appellants earlier instituted the Other Suit No.11 of 1988 for declaration of title on the Strength of Exchange deed being No.3260 dated 28-12-60 regarding the suit land in question before the Assistant Judge, Debigonj which evident from the Additional Evidence (sworn on 30-1-22) that the said suit was dismissed ex-party by the trial Court by its judgment and order dated 29-4-89 with findings—

So, the first ground does not come to play, rather, this ground is nugatory.
23. In respect of ground No.III, it may be pointed that this ground is relating to earlier suit in which private party had filed the suit. However, at present case, the Deputy Commissioner, Panchagarh made an enquiry at the instance of the complaint made by the local people's regarding the genuineness certificate. The inquiry report and other materials were produced before the Court vide Exhibit 7 with whole Nathi of the property, wherefrom, the lower Court found that enquiry report was genuine. So, the observation of the earlier case and facts of the present case are distinguishable which may not applicable in the present case. The decision given in earlier civil case upto High Court Division is not under challenge in the present case, rather, it is started on the basis of new enquiry and cause of action. In view of the new cause of action, the previous decision is not stand as impediment to try the case in accordance with law. Therefore, ground No.III also not helpful for the appellants.
24. The argument advanced by the learned Senior Counsel for the appellant regarding transposition of the Government from the respondent to petitioner seems to us that not the correct exposition of law. It is true at the  instance of the Government, there is no civil revision, however, it would not be out of juncture to reflect here, the real stream of conscienceless of the Government machineries because the Government has to act through its machinery which is not so active as like as private litigant, who can move promptly, freely, and fairly, rather, it is most difficult and cumbersome to activate the executive machineries and authorities to seek redress against the private litigant, the instant case is not exception to that characteristic, seeing such unusual behavioral act of the local administration only to secure the ends of justice and resolve the real controversy of the case, the learned Judge of the High Court Division applied the theory of due process to render the justice. Therefore, it cannot be said in activating of theory of due process, the High Court Division committed any legal infirmity. There is no such law that when any of the litigating party challenged the same judgment wherein the Government was made opposite party as the Government is the necessary party, not only that the Government contested the suit by filing written statement and on appeal, decree actually was passed against the Government when the Government machinery is reluctant to act in accordance with law, the Court not do incoherence in securing the justice, in other words, when due to incoherence of the Court justice not only defeat, rather, act of fraud would be legalized using the process of the Court. The Government, therefore, can be transposed as the petitioner from the opposite party to secure the justice.
25. Moreso, that transposing order was not challenged earlier, now in appeal raised the said ground. In appeal may raise the same as ground, however, in our view that transposition of the Government from the opposite party to petitioner by the High Court Division was not illegal, because, there is cogent and well reasonings to transpose the opposite party Government as to petitioner to resolve the real dispute in question once for all.
26. The learned Senior Counsel for the appellant raised another pertinent question whether Executive can review the judicial decision pending civil revision in the High Court Division. There is no ambiguity or any hesitation to say that according to our constitutional scheme, there is no such scope, rather, the Constitution has empowered and approved the judiciary to examine, explain and interpret the executive decision by judicial review in accordance with law. Now, in the present case, question is whether there is such occasion, is the executive reviewed the decision of judiciary? From the facts of earlier case it appears that earlier some private person filed the suit for declaration that the deed of transfer being No.4398 dated 30-7-1979 executed and registered by the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Panchagarh in favour of the defendant Nos.1-4 is collusive, fictitious, illegal, void, not acted upon and that the plaintiffs are not bound by that transfer deed along with declaration of the plaintiffs' title over the suit land. In that suit, the Government was defendant with the present appellants, not only that Government was the executor of the said deed. Therefore, the Government had supported the case of the present appellants with good faith that power of attorney and deed of exchange being Deed No.3260 of 1960 between the appellants predecessors Khandakar Nurul Islam and others with Shochida Nanda Sarkar was genuine and true, hence, registered the deed No.4398 dated 30-7-1979. So, that cannot be questioned by the third party leassees, this was the correct decision of the High Court Division in the earlier revision.
<u>27. Now, in the present case, the factssheet and scenario just opposite to the earlier facts sheet of the case because after an enquiry by the Deputy Commissioner, Panchagarh, it was unveiled that the deed of exchange being Deed No.3260 of 1960 on what basis the present Deed No.4398 dated 30-7-1979 was made and obtained by the predecessors of the plaintiffs-appellants that was forged and no land was exchanged by that deed between the above parties. Thus, it was obligatory to the Deputy Commissioner, Panchagarh to pass an appropriate order regarding that deed. Accordingly, the Deputy Commissioner passed the order and cancelled the deed in view of the prevailing condition given in the deed itself empowering the Deputy Commissioner to determine the deed if it is found that any fraud practice has been occurred in obtaining the deed from the Government. Now, the question is whether the order of cancelling the deed is genuine or not, if it was found that cancellation is not genuine on the basis of enquiry in that score, it can say that the executive acted illegally defying the earlier judgment and order of the Court of law but if it is established that earlier events the predecessors of the appellants had practiced fraud in obtaining the deed in question that unveiled after proper enquiry, in our view that it is not review of the earlier judicial discussion and decision, rather, passed the order in view of new cause of action which within the dominion of the executive. Had it been discovered in the earlier occasion that fraud practice was committed in obtaining the deed in question? Can the predecessors of the appellants can get the decree in their favour under the judicial review, the answer is obviously no. In this regard this Division's view is that the legislature, executive and judiciary have to function with their own spheres demarcated under the Constitution. No organ can usurp the functions assigned to another. Function of democracy depends upon the strength of independency of State organs. Legislature and executive have the powers maintenance, distribution and control of finance of the State. Judiciary has the power to examine and to ensure that aforesaid two organs of the State functionaries have been working within their constitutional limits and in accordance with law. The Constitution does not permit the Court to direct or advice the executive in the matter of policy or to sermonize qua any matter which under the Constitution lies within the sphere of legislature or executive, provided these authorities do not transgress their constitutional limits or statutory powers. Judiciary also must guard against encroaching the limitations. The scope of Judicial enquiry is confined to the question whether the decision taken by the Government is against any statutory provisions or is violative of the fundamental rights of the citizens or is opposed to the provisions of the Constitution. It is the executive and legislature who are entitled to frame policies and take such administrative decision as they think necessary in the public interest. The Court should not ordinarily interfere with policy decisions, unless clearly illegal or unconstitutional.</u>
28. We are, therefore, of the considered view that the submission advanced by the learned Senior Counsel is of devoid of merit.
29. In the present case from the materials on record specially from the certified copy of the deed No.3260 of 1960 it clearly divulged that the predecessors of the appellants were not got the property by exchange of their own property, rather, on cross-examination it revealed that so many inexistent events are present in the deed in question which were admitted by the PW 1. The Deputy Commissioner before filing the suit by an enquiry found that genuineness certificate was obtained by dint of a deed which was not genuine, therefore, in accordance with the condition of the deed, he cancelled the deed in question. Challenging that cancellation order the appellants had filed the suit which was dismissed by the trial Court and reversed by the Appellate Court. Again on revision, the High Court Division reversed the judgment of lower appellate Court restoring the judgment of the trial Court who dismissed the suit. Now what will be the position if the instant appeal is not allowed?
30. Now, we shall scan the evidence of the respective parties.
31. Mr Khandakar Nurul Islam, son of Khandakar Abdul Gani was examined as PW No.1 in the present suit. He made the testimonies in support of the plaint case. He testified that we have got the suit land by way of exchange on 28th December, 1960 which was belonged to Shachida Nanda Sarkar. We gave 62 Bigas land by a registered deed to Shachida Nanda Sarkar and he executed a power of attorney in favour of us. Then the power of attorney was made valid and authenticated at Rangpur. We took possession of the suit land and began to possess the same. Thus, it is admitted that the plaintiffs got suit property through exchange from Shachida Nanda Sarkar. But the original deed was never produced before the any Court. In cross he replied that it is not within in the column of signature who is the recipient of the deed. There is a pen through in the first page of the certified copy. No signature in the next page, there is a pen through in the 2nd, 3rd and 4th page. There is no signature of the sub-Registrar or anybody in the 3rd and 4th pages. There is a pen through in the next page but no signature. He cannot say from whom the stamp paper of this deed was purchased. In the opposite page of the 1st page of the stamp date is written 1.9-3-68 which is eligible. In the first page of the said deed under the signature of the sub-Registrar date written 28-2-60 but in the last page under the signature of the joint sub-Registrar, Jalpaiguri and seal is pen through and in place of 23-12-60 the date 17-5-68 was written. Shachida Nanda signed in Bengali in the deed but in the certified copy his signature is in English. To prove the certified copy, we did not file any application through High Commissioner of India nor did we call for the deed in question. He did not file any application to proof the deed by calling the relative of the Shachida Nanda Sarkar nor summoned any of them. The stamp of deed is Pakistani who and how the stamp was collected? Could not say. In the said unregistered deed Shachida Nanda Sarker signed in English but none of us signed in the deed. Writing ink of the pages are different, the date 13-9-67 is written under the signature of the Shachida Nanda Sarker but other witnesses have written date 28-9-60 under their signature, some of the witnesses signed in Hindi. He did not call for the claimed power of attorney and connecting Nathi. There is no mentioning in the deed of exchange under what Mouza of India we have exchanged the land with Bangladesh land. He denied the suggestions that they are not in possession of the suit land or there is Government House, Godown, and Graveyard.
32. The PW 2 Mr Md Nazir Uddin deposed in favour of the plaintiffs' case and their possession, plaintiffs' residing in the homestead of the Shachida Nanda Sarker. In cross he admitted that in the suit land there is some Government's Godown, Residence of the Government physicians, the graveyard, Madrasha is situated in the land of Shachida Nanda Sarkar. He cannot say by whom Bargaders the plaintiffs possessed the suit land.
33. PW 3 Mr Nozrul Islam deposed in support of the Plaintiffs' case, however, in cross he admitted that the land of Shachida Nanda Sarkar was vested property earlier and leased out to the leasees for 5 years. The plaintiffs' resides in Debiganj, then said that they reside in the house of Shachida Nanda Sarkar and Nurul Islam alone reside in Debiganj. He could not say the plot and khatian number of the suit land. He further admitted that Government's Godown of Debiganj is situated on the Government land, all the side land of Godown are land of Shachida Nanda Sarkar. There are many houses in the land of Shachida Nanda Sarkar which is adjacent to Government's Godown, there is a Graveyard in the land of Shachida Nanda Sarkar.
34. In view of the testimonies of PW Nos.1- 3, we have perused the exchange deed being Deed No.3260 of the year 1960 which has been submitted by the respondent No.10(i) as additional evidence dated 12-4-2022. On perusal of the title deed, we find that the submission advanced by the learned Advocate Mr Zulfiqur Ahmed on behalf of the respondent No.10(i), the instant deed not in the name of the Khandakar Nurul Isalm and between the Shachida Nanda Sarkar, rather, from the recital of the aforesaid deed, it transpires that deed was executed by Sree Dherendra Chandra Ghosh, son of Showrandra Chandra Ghosh of village: Jalpaiguri town, Thana and District: Jalpaiguri and purchaser was Romesh Chandra Bhowmic, son of Sree Robini Kanto Bhowmic of village: Jalpaiguri town, P.S. and District: Jalpaiguri. From the schedule it also transpires that land has described from the Collectorate of Jalpaiguri including the land of settlement Jarip No.1/770 in Khatian No.1 measuring 614 decimals of land and another land bearing settlement jarip and Hal Khatian No.1355 and Dag No.565/13 measuring 13 decimals of land which is quite different land from the land of the present suit. The aforesaid deed is not a deed of exchange; rather, it is out and out sale deed.
35. It also further reveals that Khandakar Nurul Islam and others, predecessor of the appellants as plaintiffs filed the Title Suit No.11 /88 against the Upazilla Food Officer, Debigonj and others, praying for declaration of title in the suit land describing the property in the schedule as described in the present suit's schedule.
36. It appears from the order No.34 dated 29-4-89 that suit was dismissed, holding that the deed of exchange and power of attorney are forged and fabricated documents. However, against that judgment and decree dated 29-4-89, no appeal was preferred in the higher Court by the plaintiffs.
37. The appellant's earlier also filed an execution case bearing Execution Case No.2 of 1999 for having execution of decree recovering the possession of the suit property of Other Class Suit No.17 of 1993 and Appeal No.12 of 1995 arises out from the above Other Class suit date of disposal 29-4-1995 and 5-6-1996 respectfully from which it is proved that the appellants are not in possession of the suit property except the homestead of Shachida Nanda Sarkar measuring approximately 3(three) bigas of land. Had the present appellants are in possession of total property obviously he did not file the execution case for recovery of maximum portion of the land.
<u>38. This Division from the long line of catena in the view that the plaintiff must prove his own case, for the defect of the defence case, the plaintiff cannot get any decree. Our this view is find support to the case of Abani Mohan Saha vs Assistant Custodian (SDO) vested Property, Chandpur and others reported in 39 DLR (AD) 223. This Division has held that—</u>
<u>"the plaintiff is claiming his title to the suit land on the basis of a deed of gift. I have got no doubt in my mind that the initial onus was on him to prove his title. The observation made in 32 DLR (AD) 29 would be of no avail to the appellant, as he failed to discharge his initial onus by proving his document of title. Had he succeeded to do so then the onus would have shifted on the enemy property authority to prove that the executants of the plaintiff's document, the sons of Surendra Mohan Saha, were residing in an enemy at the relevant time."</u>
39. From the above facts and circumstances of the case it appears that the plaintiffs had failed to prove the case, rather, the trial Court dismissed the suit in view of the findings given thereon. The lower appellate Court without controverting the material facts as found in the evidences and discussed by the trial Court allowed the appeal. Thereafter, the High Court Division made the Rule absolute reversing the judgment of the lower appellate Court dismissing the suit.
40. Mr Probir Neogi, the learned Senior Counsel for the appellants was asked to reply about the aforesaid documents, judgment, decree and other papers produced by the respondent No.10(i) as additional evidences. However, he frankly submits that he has no submission about those documents and failed to submit the original copy of the Deed No.3260 of 1960.
41. Mr Neogi, the learned Senior Counsel for the appellants referred before us the following precedents and relying upon those precedents prayed for allowing the appeal. The precedents, i.e. to the case of Syed Mohammad Salem Azam and others vs Bangladesh and others reported in 47 DLR (AD) 38 (Pages:1-2); Hashem (Md) vs Bangladesh and others reported in 43 DLR (1991) 109 (pages:3-4); Tarak Chandra Majhi vs Atahar Ali Howlader reported in 8 BLC (AD) 67 (pages:5-7); Haider-un-Nessa and another vs Monowara Begum and others reported in 1996 BLD (AD) 280; (page:8); Habibur Rahman Bhuiyan (Md) and others vs Galman Begum and others reported in 64 DLR (AD) 133; Shamser Ali (Md) and others vs Mosammat Kafizan Bibi reported in 44 DLR (AD) 231 (pages:20-21); Satyadhyan Ghosal and others vs Smf. Deorajin Debi and another reported in AIR 1960 (SC) 941 (pages:22- 26).
42. We have perused the above decisions, on perusal it appears to us that we have no reasons to disagree with those decisions, rather, we are respectful argument with those decisions, however, those are not helpful for the present appellants and applicable in this case because facts of the appellants' case and facts of those referred cases are quite distinguishable.
43. Contrariwise, Mr Zulfiqur Ahmed referred the case of Government of Bangladesh and another vs Mashiur Rahman and others reported in 50 DLR (AD) 205 (para-18) appears to us these precedents are squarely applicable for the present appeal, the para No.18 runs as follows:
"18.—It is a cardinal principle of administration of justice that no result of any judicial proceeding should be allowed to receive judicial approval from any Court of law whenever it is obtained by practicing fraud upon the court; reason being fraud demolishes the very foundation of sanctity of such judicial proceeding. It is also well established principle of law that fraud vitiates all judicial proceedings. Thus contravention of the provision of law cannot be a valid ground for allowing an order obtained by fraud to stand. When the trial Court itself on consideration of the materials on record was satisfied that a fraud had been committed in obtaining the ex-parte decree it was the duty of the trial Court to set-aside the ex-parte decree. The failure of the trial Court in the performance of its legal obligations ought not to have been maintained by the High Court Division in affirming the finding of the trial Court."
44. It reveals from the factsheet of the present case that it is undeniable admission from all the parties that Shachida Nanada Sarkar was the original owner of the suit property who left the erstwhile East Pakistan in the year 1960 migrating India who never came back from India to the then East Pakistan or Bangladesh. The property in question was taken over by the then administration on behalf of the State. Thereafter, some property was leased out to some persons. After that the whole property was transferred to the predecessors of the appellants. Before that, few official buildings were constructed over some portions of the property and those offices till now running by the Government official. In the meantime, the earlier lessees of the Government also claiming their possession over the suit property. The facts also revealed that the predecessors of the present appellants also claiming that they are in possession of the suit property but not in accordance with law.
45. From the above facts and circumstances and materials on record, we are of the view that the predecessor of the appellants had practiced fraud at the time of obtaining genuineness certificate dated 29-4-1989 and thereby fraudently obtained the Deed being Deed No.4389 dated 25-8-1989.
46. In view of the above, we are of the view that the High Court Division in making the Rule absolute committed no error of law which does not call for interference by this Division.
47. Now another pertinent question arises what would be the position of the property and who will be the owner of the properties. Since, it is manifestly proved that the property originally belonged to Sochida Nanda Sarkar and he left for India keeping the property concerned without living any heirs in this Country and never come back to this Country. We are of the opinion that in such situation clause (c) of sub-article (1) of the Article 143 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh will come into play which runs as follows.
"Property of the Republic"
143.—(1)There shall vest in the Republic, in addition to any other land or property lawfully vested—
a) all minerals and other things of value underlying any land of Bangladesh;
b) all lands, minerals and other things of value underlying the ocean within the territorial waters, or the ocean over the continental shelf, of Bangladesh; and
c) any property located in Bangladesh  that has no rightful owner.
48. In view of the above provision of the Constitution the whole properties owner is the Republic of Bangladesh.
49. It may be mentioned here that the predecessor of the appellants are in possession of the homestead of Shachida Nanda Sarkar from the year 1960 and from the evidence it appears that such possession was not denied by the Government, respondent Nos.1-2. Since appellants and their predecessors are/were in possession of the homestead of Shachida Nanda Sarkar since long, we are, therefore, of the view that the landed property belonged to the appellants i.e. homestead of Shachida Nanda Sarkar measuring 3(three) bighas, the appellants for ends of justice would be entitled to have permanent lease because the predecessors of the appellants were refugees to take shelter came from India. The lease money would be Taka 1,00,000 (Taka one lac) only.
50. The defendant respondent Nos.1-5 is directed to execute the lease deed in favour of the plaintiff appellants in accordance with law within 6(six) months from the communication of this judgment positively.
51. In the result, the Civil Appeal is dismissed without any order as to cost.
Let a copy of this judgment communicate to the Deputy Commissioner, Panchagor for necessary steps.
End.

(Arising out of C.P. No.1351 of 2018)

Mr. Samarandra Nath Biswas, Deputy Attorney General, instructed by Mrs. Sufia Khatun, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Appellants
Mr. Mohammad Yusuf Hossain Humayun, Senior Advocate with Mohammad Hossain, Advocate instructed by Mr. Zainul Abedin, Advocate-on-Record ---------- For the Respondents
